author: Subscriptor
body:
After being a Jr Moderator and experiencing this issue myself and seeing others deal with it, I have came to a conclusion that this problem needs to be solved.

What's the problem?: Moderators cannot IP check or review and deal with online appeals.

What is it leading to?:The fact that we have a low number of senior mods decreases the staff team's effeciency significantly, and makes moderators being really dependant on senior moderators on a part of their job. On slack, moderators always request senior moderators to do an IP check or deal with an appeal. The senior moderators are not always on slack and in game. As well as their low number just justifies the problem. I have seen many times myself when I or others request to IP check and it can take to a whole hour untill a senior staff member responds. This whole cases leads to situations as a hacker ban evading multiple times and cannot be IP checked by moderators because no seniors are on, moderators constantly asking on slack the seniors to deal with an ignored appeal, etc.

What can we do about that?: There are 2 solutions that I see at the moment. First - Increasing the number of senior moderators. Second, Giving the moderators the ability to IP check and deal with appeals themselves.

What are the advantages and the disadvantages of these solutions?: 
Solution number 1 - Increasing the number of Senior Moderators:
Pros:
- This will give a chance to moderators that have been moderators for a very long time and want to redeem themselves and become a senior moderators. There are quite a few of these actually. 
- Will increase the effeciency of the report/appeal/IPcheck system.
Cons:
- Making the senior staff team bigger will lead to a mess. I personally dislike the idea of a bigger senior staff team.
- More Senior Moderaotrs ==> More moderators. I assume that increasing the number of senior moderators will lead to an increasement on the moderators team. In my opinion, to such a small server it's a problem.
- Moderators still stay dependant on the senior moderators.
Solution number 2 - Giving moderators the ability to IP check and deal with appeals themselves:
Pros:
- This will significantly increase the effeciency of the staff team as a whole, no more players waiting for punishments or their appeals to be dealt for such a long time.
- Will give moderators more options and tools that they will experience in their time as a moderator.
- Moderators will no longer be dependant on senior much like before.
Cons:
- Not all moderators are trustworhy and giving them these permissions can lead to abuse situations.
- Since moderators are not experienced with dealing with appeals this might lead to unfair judgement or bias.

Tell me your opinion.

replies.author: Ironsoldier2000
replies.body:
Moderators will never be allowed to IPCheck as IPChecks contain HIGHLY sensitive information. Things that 30 people should not see. (IP's) Secondly, we are currently working on improving the appeal system. Finally, having more than 11 senior mods is detrimental to the OVERALL efficiency of the team. Having more than 11 seniors causes huge delays in productivity, AND we can only promote people who excel the role. Making promoting an excess of 6/7 hard.

That's just my two cents. Take it as you wish.

replies.author: hasl
replies.body:
The step from the moderator position to senior is huge. You have acces to the chat logs, IP lists, ability to web ban and deal with appeals, as well as many more. I feel people see the jump as pretty average, but it's not and you can't just resolve a problem like this with "just promote more moderators" because then you have a bunch of unexpirienced, useless seniors. 

So that rules that idea out.

I don't know how active !ipcheck is in #requests, but I remember an average of about three to four an hour at peak. However, if the amount of IP checks has risen significantly, then I guess letting moderators have access to it would be ok, but training for it would be a right pain. 

I would prefer you guys to let the senior staff handle it, there is at least one active senior in each continent, excluding Europe. *cough* ^.^ *cough*

Because I'm pretty sure that's what I've seen and if that is the case then it really isn't sensitive information.

You did bring up good points about the appeal system. but it shouldn't be relevant soon as it is currently being revamped and improved as we speak, so I would give that a few weeks (hopefully) until after the new system is implemented.

EDIT: Also if moderators are trusted to ban people, why would they would abuse ipchecks. If we can't be trusted with those then we shouldn't be part of the staff team.

replies.author: Crazy_
replies.body:
How come moderators can't deal with their own appeals? As a mod on OCN (where we do deal with our own appeals), I can't imagine how much work that creates for Sr staff. 

Over on OCN we have a simple way with dealing with appeals. Of course, the system is different, which makes some of it easier. But anyways, a player creates the appeal, the moderator then provides any proof they have, and choose whether or not to accept or deny the appeal. If a player feels like the mod is bias/not good at determining hacks, or not responding, they can escalate the appeal for the Sr staff to deal with (they also escalate for other reason, but those are the common ones).

In terms of IP checks, mods shouldn't have the ability to check those, for reasons stated above.
